newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI EARNS FOURTH STRAIGHT INDYCAR POLE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ZANARDI EARNS FOURTH STRAIGHT INDYCAR POLE.

text.p: Italian Alessandro Zanardi's best lap was his last lap as he grabbed his fourth straight IndyCar pole at the Laguna Seca Raceway on Saturday.
Zanardi, in his rookie year in the series, won his sixth pole, more than any other driver this year, heading into the final IndyCar race of the season.
He drove his Reynard Honda around the 11-turn, 2.238-mile (3.602 km) circuit in northern Calfornia in a time of 68.004 seconds for a course qualifying record speed of 118.475 mph (190.661 kph).

"As I drove into the first turn," Zanardi said, "somebody put a wheel off the circuit and threw up some dust. I was a little demoralised because I knew I had only one lap left. Except for that first turn it was a perfect lap."

Herta, an American who drives a Reynard Mercedes-Benz, was unable to improve his Friday clocking of 68.019 seconds and fell to second place followed by Brazilian Mauricio Gugelmin, who qualified third at 68.188 seconds in a Reynard Ford Cosworth.

Meanwhile, series points leader Jimmy Vasser's hopes for his first IndyCar championship brightened when he qualified fifth fastest while his chief rivals, Michael Andretti and Al Unser Jr, were only 11th and 13th.

"Anything can happen in this race," said Vasser, a northern California native. "Both of those guys are capable of coming from anywhere in the pack to win the race. We still have to drive as hard as we can".
With a 14-point lead over Andretti and 17-point lead over Unser, Vasser can clinch the championship with a fifth-place finish or better no matter where his rivals finish.
"This is a tough track to pass on," said Andretti. "I have to go for it and win the race. I have to finish in at least third place if Vasser drops out."
Said Unser: "Jimmy is going to be tough to shake and Michael will be there too. This race will be a fight to the finish."
Twenty-nine drivers will start Sunday's 83-lap, 185.976-mile (299.291 km) IndyCar series finale.
